extracted.intended_audience: Institutions, authorized organizational officials (AORs), investigators, subrecipients, and research administrators applying for or managing NIH grants
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and evaluative requirements from the NIH Grants Policy Statement covering financial conflicts of interest (FCOI), Fly America Act, health and safety, biospecimen security, stem cell and fetal tissue research, and human subjects protections that applicants and recipients must follow to obtain and maintain NIH funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value reporting increments for financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Value of the financial interest $0-4,999; $5,000-9,999; $10,000-19,999; amounts between $20,000-100,000 by increments of $20,000; amounts above $100,000 by increments of $50,000 or a statement that a value cannot be readily determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these increments when reporting the dollar value of significant financial interests (SFIs); if value cannot be readily determined, state that. (Context: part of required FCOI disclosure content.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of how the financial interest relates to NIH-funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: A description how the financial interest relates to NIH-funded research and the basis for the Institution’s determination that the financial interest conflicts with such research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide narrative linking the SFI to the specific NIH-funded project and explain why the Institution determined the SFI constitutes an FCOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management plan: role and principal duties of conflicted Investigator
rubrics_metrics.description: Role and principal duties of the conflicted Investigator in the research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific responsibilities the conflicted Investigator will have under the award so reviewers and NIH can assess risk and mitigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management plan: conditions of the management plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Conditions of the management plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify restrictions, disclosures, divestiture, oversight, or other conditions imposed to manage the FCOI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management plan: how plan safeguards objectivity
rubrics_metrics.description: How the management plan is designed to safeguard objectivity in the research project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain mechanisms (e.g., independent monitoring, data access controls) that will protect design, conduct, and reporting from bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management plan: confirmation of Investigator agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirmation of the Investigator’s agreement to the management plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document Investigator acknowledgement/acceptance of the management plan terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management plan: monitoring to ensure Investigator compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: How the management plan will be monitored to ensure Investigator compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe monitoring frequency, responsible parties, reporting, and corrective actions for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management plan: other information as needed
rubrics_metrics.description: Other information as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include any additional details necessary for NIH to understand and evaluate the adequacy of the management plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual FCOI report timing and submission channel
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual FCOI report must be submitted to NIH through the eRA Commons FCOI Module each year within a competitive segment or until the Institution reports that the FCOI no longer exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit annually via eRA Commons for the duration of the competitive segment (or until FCOI resolved).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual FCOI report required content
rubrics_metrics.description: The annual FCOI report will include the following information: status of the FCOI; changes to the management plan, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should clearly state whether the FCOI remains and document any modifications to management measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium/subrecipient written agreement content
rubrics_metrics.description: The agreement must establish whether the FCOI policy of the recipient Institution or that of the subrecipient will apply to subrecipient Investigators and in either case, the agreement must include required significant financial interest disclosure, review, and FCOI reporting timelines to ensure compliance with the FCOI regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal written agreements signed by recipient and subrecipient must specify which policy governs and include timelines and disclosure/review procedures to enable compliance and timely NIH reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subrecipient reporting timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Subrecipient Institutions who rely on their FCOI policy must report identified FCOIs to the recipient Institution in sufficient time to allow the recipient Institution to report the FCOI to NIH to meet its reporting obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure subrecipients’ reporting cadence allows lead recipient to meet NIH reporting deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH right to request written agreements and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH reserves the right to request copies of the written agreement and relevant supporting documentation as needed as part of its oversight responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide requested documentation may lead to remedies for noncompliance and potential enforcement actions (see remedies and conditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of FCOI information for senior/key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institution will make certain information available concerning identified FCOI held by senior/key personnel via a publicly accessible web site or by a written response to any requestor within five business days of a request and update such information as specified in the regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a public display or produce written responses within five business days and keep information current per regulatory specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional FCOI policy maintenance and posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Institution shall maintain an up-to-date, written, enforced policy on FCOI that complies with the regulation, and make the policy available via a publicly accessible web site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must submit their publicly accessible FCOI policy to NIH via the eRA Commons Institution Profile (IPF) Module; policy is institutional-level information, not grant-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator SFI disclosure requirement (domestic and foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institution must require each Investigator to disclose their (and their spouse and dependent children) domestic and foreign SFIs that are related to their Institutional responsibilities to the Institution’s designated official(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures must include family members' interests; institution must collect disclosures tied to institutional responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure of foreign financial interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators must disclose all foreign financial interests (which includes income from seminars, lectures, or teaching engagements, income from service on advisory committees or review panels, and reimbursed or sponsored travel) received from any foreign entity when such income meets the threshold for disclosure (e.g., income in excess of $5,000).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include income and reimbursed travel from foreign entities; institutions are encouraged to review FCOI policies to ensure investigators understand disclosure responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator FCOI training frequency and triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Institution must require each Investigator (including subrecipient Investigators) to complete training prior to engaging in NIH-supported research and at least every four years, and immediately under the designated circumstances: institutional FCOI policies change; an Investigator is new to an Institution; an Institution finds an Investigator noncompliant with the Institution’s FCOI policy or management plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide initial and periodic refresher training; require immediate retraining when policy changes, new hires, or noncompliance occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of acceptable FCOI management measures
rubrics_metrics.description: As described in the regulation, examples of how FCOIs might be managed include but are not limited to: public disclosure of FCOI; disclosure of FCOI directly to human subjects research participants; monitoring of research by independent reviewer(s); modification of the research plan; change of personnel or personnel responsibilities, or disqualification of personnel from participation in all or a portion of the research; reduction or elimination of SFIs (e.g., sale of an equity interest); severance of relationships that create FCOIs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these measures as examples when designing management plans; selection should be appropriate to the nature and magnitude of the risk to objectivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fly America Act general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fly America Act (49 U.S.C. 40118) generally provides that foreign air travel funded by Federal government money may only be conducted on U.S. flag air carriers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A “U.S. flag air carrier” is an air carrier that holds a certificate under 49 U.S.C. 41102; foreign carriers operating under a permit are not U.S. flag air carriers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible use of foreign-flag air carriers (Fly America exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited circumstances under which use of a foreign-flag air carrier is permissible, including: (1) Airline 'Open Skies' Agreement coverage; (2) involuntary rerouting; (3) Travel To and From the U.S. where using U.S.-flag carriers would extend travel time by specified thresholds; (4) Travel Between Points Outside the U.S. under certain connection/time conditions; (5) Short Distance Travel where elapsed scheduled flight time is three hours or less and U.S.-flag service would double travel time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients and contractors must check airline coverage under Open Skies agreements and follow the detailed timing/connection rules; consult GSA guidance and Fly America Act resources for specifics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient responsibility for health and safety standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are responsible for meeting applicable Federal, State, and local health and safety standards and for establishing and implementing necessary measures to minimize their employees’ risk of injury or illness in activities related to NIH grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to law, follow OSHA standards (e.g., 29 CFR Part 1910.1030 and 1910.1450) and other applicable regulations; be prepared to provide evidence of implementation if requested by awarding IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable regulatory and recommended safety guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow applicable occupational health and safety standards (OSHA 29 CFR Part 1910), Nuclear Regulatory Commission Standards, and recommended guidelines such as Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL) and Prudent Practices for Safety in Laboratories (2011).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended publications provide practical procedures for lab safety; recipients should consider and implement appropriate practices even though documented assurance is not routinely required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of health and safety compliance on request
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested by the awarding IC, recipients should be able to provide evidence that applicable Federal, State, and local health and safety standards have been considered and have been put into practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records and evidence of safety procedures and implementation for potential audits or oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH Biospecimens Security Policy applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: As of October 24, 2025, NIH recipients must comply with the NIH Policy on Enhancing Security Measures for Human Biospecimens. The Policy applies to ongoing or new NIH funding instruments used to obtain human clinical and research biospecimens from U.S. persons (regardless of identifiability), that are collected, obtained, stored, used, or distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy does not apply to cell derivative products or cell lines derived from human biospecimens of U.S. persons that were commercially or publicly available prior to October 24, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on distributing NIH-funded U.S. persons' biospecimens to countries of concern
rubrics_metrics.description: The entity that holds human biospecimens of U.S. persons collected, obtained, stored, used, or distributed using ongoing or new NIH funds are prohibited from directly or indirectly distributing the human biospecimens to institutions or parties located in countries of concern (as defined under 28 CFR § 202.601).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize the risks of sharing biospecimens with countries of concern; NIH expects recipients to limit sharing consistent with the Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited exceptions for sharing biospecimens with countries of concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Human biospecimens may be shared or distributed to countries of concern only if: (1) to meet transactions required or authorized by Federal law or international agreements; (2) needed in rare and compelling circumstances where the foreign facility/personnel possess unique capabilities/ expertise not available elsewhere and with donor consent; or (3) at the request of the individual whose biospecimen was collected for their diagnosis/treatment and in compliance with applicable laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sharing under an exception, recipients must document the justification and retain records of quantity and content as required; exports must follow applicable export administration regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping requirement for biospecimen sharing to countries of concern
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH requires all recipients to retain documentation related to sharing or distributing biospecimens to countries of concern under allowable limited circumstances and further document the quantity and content of the biospecimen material that was shared or distributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per 2 C.F.R. Part 200.337 (Access to Records), recipients must provide these records to NIH upon request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human embryonic stem cell (hESC) use and registry requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH recipients may use hESCs that have been approved by NIH in accord with NIH Guidelines and are posted on the NIH Human Embryonic Stem Cell Registry, or may establish eligibility of specific cell lines for NIH funding by submitting NIH Form 2890.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must provide assurances that hESCs to be used are listed on the Registry or provide a strong justification and certification that a Registry-listed line will be used prior to use of NIH funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibited uses of human pluripotent stem cells with NIH funding
rubrics_metrics.description: The following uses of hESCs or human induced pluripotent stem cells are prohibited: research in which hESCs or iPSCs are introduced into non-human primate blastocysts; research involving the breeding of animals where introduction of hESCs or iPSCs may contribute to the germ line; derivation of stem cells from human embryos (Dickey-Wicker restrictions); and introducing human pluripotent cells into non-human vertebrate pre-gastrulation stage embryos.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not seek NIH funding for the listed prohibited activities; consult NIH Guidelines and law for other limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human fetal tissue (HFT) statutory requirements and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Human fetal tissue is defined as tissue or cells obtained from a dead human embryo or fetus after a spontaneous or induced abortion or stillbirth. Sections 498A and 498B of the PHS Act set forth specific requirements and prohibitions on research involving human fetal tissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Familiarize with statutory prohibitions (e.g., no acquiring/receiving/transferring for valuable consideration) and additional regulatory requirements including informed consent and documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Informed consent and documentation for HFT
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH expects informed consent to have been obtained from the donor for any NIH-funded research using human fetal tissue, and recipients must maintain appropriate documentation when obtaining primary human fetal tissue for research purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain records supporting proper informed consent and be prepared to make them available for audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requirements for transplantation research using HFT
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on transplantation of HFT must adhere to provisions including: donor woman's signed statement (donation for therapeutic transplantation research; no restriction on recipient identity; donor unaware of recipient identity); attending physician statements about obtaining tissue and disclosures; for induced abortions, physician statements that abortion consent preceded tissue consent, timing/method not altered for tissue collection, and abortion complied with state law; PD/PI certifications regarding awareness and noninvolvement in abortion timing/method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AOR signing the application certifies availability of physician statements, PD/PI statements, and informed consents for audit; violations carry criminal penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH prohibition on research using HFT from elective abortions (effective Jan 22, 2026)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective January 22, 2026, NIH funds are not permitted for research using HFT from elective abortions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not propose or expect NIH funding for research using HFT obtained from elective abortions after this effective date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protections: applicability of 45 CFR Part 46 and FWA requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions engaged in nonexempt research involving human subjects must comply with 45 CFR Part 46, provide written assurance by obtaining a Federalwide Assurance (FWA) with OHRP, and establish appropriate policies and procedures for protection of human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An institution is 'engaged' if it intervenes or interacts with subjects, obtains identifiable information or biospecimens, or receives a direct HHS award to conduct human subjects research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special population protections (Subparts B, C, D)
rubrics_metrics.description: The HHS regulations at Subparts B, C, and D include additional protections for pregnant women, human fetuses and neonates (Subpart B); prisoners (Subpart C); and children (Subpart D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When research involves these populations, follow the specific additional requirements in the cited Subparts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional procedures for exemption determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutions must adopt clear procedures under which the IRB (or some authority other than the investigator) determines whether proposed research is exempt from the human subjects regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH will review materials and may concur with exemption claims, but institution retains full regulatory responsibility for correct determinations and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: FWA and IRB registration/coverage for performance sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient institution must file its own FWA even if it designates another IRB; organizations that will serve as additional performance sites engaged in nonexempt research must obtain an FWA or may, under specified circumstances, be covered by the recipient's FWA per OHRP guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all participating sites are covered by appropriate FWA arrangements before commencing nonexempt human subjects research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on commencement of human subjects research without FWA/IRB approval
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH awarding component will place a restriction in the Notice of Award so that no human subjects research may be conducted under the award until the FWA and certification of IRB review and approval (or certification of institutional determination of exemption) have been obtained and accepted by NIH.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not begin human subjects activities until NIH has accepted required FWA and IRB certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of IRB approval: final approval required (no conditional approvals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients must provide a certification to NIH that all nonexempt research involving human subjects has been reviewed and approved by an appropriate IRB. NIH requires the date of final IRB approval; conditional IRB approval is not sufficient. IRB approval with conditions only becomes effective when the IRB has approved all information submitted in response to their conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting documentation to NIH, include the date of final IRB approval; do not rely on conditional approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed onset human subjects research requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If human subjects research is anticipated within the period of the award but definite plans cannot be described ('delayed onset'), applicants must provide a detailed explanation of why definite plans cannot be developed. Prior to involvement of human subjects, the recipient must submit to the NIH awarding IC either (1) detailed information required in the PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information Form and meet FWA and IRB certification requirements, or (2) identification of applicable exemptions(s) with justification and sufficient information to allow determination that the claimed exemption is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow awarding IC procedures for adding protocols and obtain prior approvals for new protocols; recipients may not draw funds or obligate funds for human subjects research at sites without FWA and IRB approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of IRB review costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs associated with IRB review of human research protocols are not allowable as direct charges to NIH-funded research unless such costs are not covered by the organization’s indirect cost rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan budgets accordingly; request clarification if IRB costs are not covered by indirect rates.
